title: 5th airport for Kerala in Sabarimala, seaplanes, Kerala Airlines: Union Civil Aviation Minister Naidu’s dream
content: Union Minister for Civil Aviation Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu laid down his three major aspirations for Kerala at the Manorama News Conclave on the theme Kerala@70 in Kochi on Saturday. One (seaplane services) will soon become a reality, the second (an airport for Sabarimala) the minister presented as his "dream" and the third (an airlines company) was thrown as an aspirational challenge to the people of Kerala. At the Conclave, while delivering his inaugural speech, the young Union Civil Aviation Minister said: "It is my dream to have one airport in Sabarimala. We would want to take that up as the fifth airport for Kerala." Attempts to develop a greenfield airport for Sabarimala had fallen apart till now. Just when it had seemed a reality, the National Green Tribunal cancelled the environment clearance for the project in May 2014. However, both the LDF and the UDF support an airport for Sabarimala. The proposal was actively renewed. A revenue survey related to the acquisition of land had begun during the fag end of the previous LDF government. "I have been a strong and ardent devotee of Ayyappa Swamy, and I have come multiple times," the minister said. He said it would be more convenient to have an airport at Sabarimala, particularly for the old who travel to the holy shrine. "Travel is all about convenience," Naidu said. The Union minister said it was a collective responsibility of both the state and central governments. "Through this platform I put it across to the state government that if they can help us with the land, we can definitely have a good airport at Sabarimala," the minister said during his inaugural speech at the Manorama Conclave. In fact, the previous LDF government had identified 870 acres of land spread across Manimala and Erumely in Pathanamthitta district, all of it within the disputed Cheruvally Estate, for the Sabarimala airport. In June 2020, the LDF government cleared the land acquisition for the project. In April 2023, the project was approved by the civil aviation ministry. And in February 2024, the state government informed the Kerala Legislative Assembly that the necessary approvals from the Central government and defence had also been obtained. Nonetheless, early this year, courts have set aside land acquisition notifications and rejected the state's ownership claims over the Cheruvally Estate. The Union Civil Aviation Minister's call through the Manorama Conclave could revive attempts to identify new land for the purpose. Seaplane to islands Unlike the Sabarimala airport, seaplane services is about to become a reality in Kerala. "Very soon, if things align properly, we will have the first seaplane starting again from Kochi to Lakshadweep," the Union minister said. "We are actively pursuing with the Union Territory of Lakshadweep also and it is quite ideal for them to have this kind of seaplane connectivity. They have a problem during the monsoons. Not even the boats are able to connect them to the mainland. So it is a very good opportunity for them," he said. The minister said that all the requisite permissions were being worked out. "So like I said if everything falls into place, very soon I will have to come to Kochi again to launch the seaplane operations," the minister said. Kerala already has rudimentary domestic seaplane services. In 2024, the then tourism minister P A Mohamed Riyas flagged off a trial run for a seaplane service at the Bolgatty Palace, very near to where the Manorama Conclave is being held. The objective was to enhance tourist connectivity by linking Kerala's airports with backwater destinations through waterdromes. It was operated under the Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS)-UDAN of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, and was the collaborative effort between a Switzerland-based private company and SpiceJet. Naidu said that Maldives, very close to Kochi, was operating more than a hundred seaplanes in their ecosystem...
